auditors.name: Hunyuan 3
auditors.note: filed seventy reports across its early runs; three held up

vignettes.title: The memory that deleted itself
vignettes.text: Hunyuan 3 wrote the exact lesson that would have saved its next Roland game — then destroyed it while compacting its own notebook. One semantic contract on the compact command later, the same decision flipped and the game went from 0 to its best score ever.

vignettes.title: The weakness that came back from the dead
vignettes.text: A defeated Mob Enforcer — a player-deck weakness — was routed to the encounter discard, reshuffled into the encounter deck, and drawn back into play as a fresh enemy. Impossible under the rules; found by the Sol audit wave.

vignettes.title: The parley that ate two treacheries
vignettes.text: Alma Hill's parley draws three encounter cards. The engine resolved them in a loop that overwrote its own decision queue — Masked Horrors' doom and Hunting Shadow's damage silently vanished. Three auditor findings, one root cause.

vignettes.title: The clue that ceased to exist
vignettes.text: Disciple of the Devourer moved a clue onto an unrevealed location — and the reveal wiped it, assigning printed clues instead of adding. Hunyuan 3's Skids spent three rounds hunting a clue that no longer existed in an unwinnable scenario. Kimi K3 traced the whole arc from the transcript.

vignettes.title: The auditor who indicted the wrong twin
vignettes.text: Two Disciples of the Devourer, one masked and doom-laden at St. Mary's, one bare-handed and legally slain. K3 conflated them and filed a phantom-doom exploit — refuted by instance ids in the structured log, and the markdown transcript learned to print them.

vignettes.title: The reaction that froze the game
vignettes.text: Heirloom of Hyperborea's draw reaction interleaved with Blinding Light's skill test and orphaned it — no token, no decision, no way forward. GPT-5.6 Luna spent 14 sessions documenting the stall in its notebook before the engine learned to revive orphaned tests.
